footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $7,943M; $7,928M of it was attributable to common stockholders and $15M to noncontrolling interests. Tesla's Q4 update letter is a slide deck, so the Q4 figures are derived from the audited full-year 2023 Form 10-K statements less the nine months ended September 30, 2023 in the Q3 2023 Form 10-Q — and every line ties exactly to the update letter's own summary table (revenue $25,167M, gross profit $4,438M, operating income $2,064M). The tax line was a $5,752M benefit, drawn as a green source into net profit (the taxben link fix used on other tax-benefit pages is applied here too).

oneTimers: One-time non-cash tax benefit of $5.9B — Tesla released the valuation allowance it had held against its deferred tax assets, judging future profits now make those assets usable. It turned $2,191M of pre-tax profit into $7,943M of net income (the total tax line was a $5,752M benefit); it is not cash and not a repeat item.
otherDetail: Interest income of $333M on cash and short-term investments, less $61M of interest expense and $145M of other expense, net — mainly foreign-exchange moves — a net +$127M.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose just 3% YoY to $25.2B — automotive revenue grew only 1% as repeated price cuts offset record deliveries of 484,507 vehicles.
takeaways.title: Revenue growth nearly stalled

takeaways.text: Net income of $7,943M includes a $5.9B one-time, non-cash tax benefit from releasing a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets. Operating income itself fell 47% YoY to $2,064M.
takeaways.title: A tax bookkeeping gain did the profit

takeaways.text: Gross margin was 17.6%, down from 23.8% a year ago, as price cuts outran cost reductions — and Tesla warned 2024 volume growth could be notably lower while it launches its next-generation vehicle.
takeaways.title: Car margins kept thinning

verdict: Tesla's revenue grew just 3% to $25.2B as price cuts squeezed car profits — but a one-time $5.9B tax benefit lifted net income to $7.9B.
